doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Joe Venuti stories at Palisades Park and the bandstand fire
summary: Marty recalls Joe Venuti as a character, including a fire built on the bandstand to roast hot dogs.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well you have played with an amazing list of people.
Did you see that list I gave you?
Yes, I’m looking at it now. I have my own little sheet here too.
Oh you have your own thing, I see.
Joe Venuti? Some really marvelous — not only musicians but characters.
Joe Venuti himself was a character. Unbelievable. I was telling a story just the other day about Joe Venuti. We played Palisades Park. Do you remember that name at all?

Palisades Park? Well when we played Palisades Park in New Jersey, Cliffside, someplace, and we used to do on Saturdays a matinee, and right across the park was an Italian restaurant. And we’d go there for dinner. And Joe knew the bosses, which didn’t matter anyway, but we would sit there and he would tell us stories, and we did more

laughing than eating because he was a very funny guy. There were stories about Joe Venuti that you don’t believe, and I’ve got some in my book that are incredible. About one where we were working at a park in Lincoln, not Nebraska, Lincoln Park in Massachusetts someplace, Bedford, Mass. Anyway, it was an outdoor park, it was an amusement park, and it was September and we were freezing. Guys were wearing overcoats and gloves. I was playing piano with gloves on, so was Joe.

No he took a chair and he broke it up and he said to the band, “go buy some weenies,” and the kid went to the store to buy the weenies and he came back and Joe took the chair and broke it up and built a fire on the bandstand. Then he took the weenies like this and he was sitting there while the band was playing and the kids were dancing, and he was roasting hot dogs, see? And the manager came running, and was furious. Because the kids, instead of dancing, they came around to watch the band. He says, “what the hell is this guy doing?” He’s cooking frankfurters. So the manager went crazy. He says, “what are you doing? Well Joe was very cool you know, and he used to look at you this way and bite his lip saying, “what’s wrong, whatsa matter?” The guy says, “what’s wrong? You’ve got a fire on the bandstand.” He says, “well the guys are freezing man, I’m trying to feed them, because we’re cold.” So he says, “you broke my chair.” Joe he got up and put his hand up and says, “how much was the chair?” He was going to pay for the chair. He was crazy. But he had such great stories, I’m telling you. I’ve got some stories in my book about him you won’t believe. You just don’t believe man.
